newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish TPSA phone firm raises prices from Feb 1.
newsitem.headline: Polish TPSA phone firm raises prices from Feb 1.

text.p: Poland's Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) telephone operator said on Tuesday it would raise on February 1 prices of local calls by one grosz per unit to 18 groszes per unit.

TPSA said in a statement that the previous rate rise in July 1996, also by one grosz, failed to make up for inflation and the rise was designed to bring prices of local phone calls closer to OECD levels.
"The price of a local phone call amounts to less than half of the OECD-average," the statement said.
TPSA said that the move was also designed to narrow the gap between the costs of local and long-distance calls.
It said long-distance calls cost 15 times as much as local calls while in OECD countries they cost 12 times more on average.

TPSA has been often criticised for its pricing policies and price structure and has been subject of Polish Anti-Monopoly Office probes which last week signalled that if TPSA decided to raise rates once again it might launch another inquiry whether the company was not abusing its near-monopoly.
